The story's Verification block and LLD §5.2 unambiguously place this file at `src/patient_360/silver/transform_patients.py`. pattern: When an AC backtick-quotes a bare filename but the story's Verification block fully qualifies the same file under a different skill domain, extract-deliverables should prefer the Verification-block path (or DELIVERABLE-OWNERS should match by basename when no slashes are present). correction: Sub-skill create-silver resolved chapter-5 as workspace and halted on its Updated-Pending-Review backlog, while chapter-6 (the orchestrator workspace) backlog was Approved. .skill-arg/.skill-paths in chapter-6 were not consumed.
pattern: When .skill-arg / .skill-paths remain present in the orchestrator workspace after a sub-skill dispatch, treat as CRITICAL workspace-ambiguity. Sub-skill discovery walked to a sibling chapter. Either pass an absolute --workspace-root flag (or env var) to the sub-skill, or detect non-consumed scoping files and halt with the explicit message: sub-skill resolved a different workspace; pass workspace-root explicitly.

correction: Generated replace_where_write() called saveAsTable() WITHOUT .option('path', ...), creating managed tables in the default Spark warehouse dir. On every re-run after a container/metastore recreation, Spark's Derby metastore was empty while Delta data remained on disk, causing DELTA_CREATE_TABLE_WITH_NON_EMPTY_LOCATION failures. The _external_table_path() helper existed in delta_helpers.py but was dead code.
pattern: Any Delta writer (Bronze/Silver/Gold) that materialises an external table MUST pass .option('path', <absolute_path>) to saveAsTable. The path MUST be computed deterministically from the table FQN via a shared helper (e.g. _external_table_path) so it survives metastore resets. Path-based external Delta is the contract per LLD §13 Decision 15 (revised 2026-05-12); managed-table semantics are forbidden because they create idempotency hazards on local embedded-Derby setups.

correction: Per-table YAML config declared `output_path: ${PATIENT360_WAREHOUSE_ROOT}/dev/bronze/<table>/` but the runner never resolved the env var nor passed the path to the writer. The configured field was silently ignored.
pattern: Any declared config field that influences runtime behavior MUST be threaded end-to-end: read in the runner, env-var-expanded if templated, passed to the helper that uses it. If a field is dead, either remove it from the config schema or wire it. Drift between declared config and actual behavior is a silent-failure source.

correction: Generated DAG started with the bronze_ingestion TaskGroup as the root, leaving the shared SE stats/errors Delta tables (`bronze.bronze_se_stats`, `bronze.bronze_se_errors`) to be CREATEd by whichever bronze task ran first. On a cold metastore, parallel siblings race the CREATE; on a recreated metastore with on-disk data, every task failed with DELTA_CREATE_TABLE_WITH_NON_EMPTY_LOCATION. The workaround `max_active_tasks=1` capped concurrency and was a known TODO in the DAG.
pattern: Every DAG that uses shared Spark-Expectations stats/errors tables MUST start with a `bootstrap_se` SparkSubmitOperator task (one short spark-submit against the SE bootstrap script) upstream of any TaskGroup that writes SE stats. The bootstrap MUST be idempotent (CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS + CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS USING DELTA LOCATION). After this task is in place, the bronze_ingestion TaskGroup MAY restore its LLD-specified concurrency (e.g. max_active_tasks=16) — the per-task concurrency cap is no longer needed for SE-table CREATE serialization.

correction: Generated docker-compose.yml mounted /opt/patient_360 subdirectories (src/contracts/dq_rules/scripts/data/_infra/cd/config) but did NOT mount /opt/patient_360/warehouse. After the LLD §13 Decision 12 pivot (2026-05-12) anchored the Hive warehouse + Derby metastore at ${PATIENT360_PROJECT_ROOT}/warehouse/{env}/, every Spark task failed with 'Failed to create database /opt/patient_360/warehouse/dev/metastore_db' because /opt/patient_360 itself is root-owned in the airflow image (drwxr-xr-x root:root) and the airflow user (uid 50000) can't create new directories there.
pattern: Every path that the runtime anchors on PATIENT360_PROJECT_ROOT (or any project root env var) MUST have a corresponding writable bind mount in docker-compose. Audit rule for create-scaffold/update-scaffold: enumerate every distinct path prefix that the runner code derives from the project-root env var (warehouse, metastore_db, quarantine, logs, etc.) and emit a matching `../../<dir>:/opt/<project>/<dir>` mount with the host dir pre-created. NEVER assume the project-root dir is writable — it is root-owned in the airflow base image.

correction: Generated Dockerfile.airflow left /opt/patient_360/ as root:root drwxr-xr-x (Docker auto-creates bind-mount-point parents as root). The airflow user (uid 50000) couldn't create the warehouse subdir at runtime; Derby failed with `Failed to create database '/opt/patient_360/warehouse/dev/metastore_db'`.
pattern: Every cookiecutter Dockerfile that bind-mounts subdirectories under a project-root path MUST also chown that project-root path to the runtime user during image build, BEFORE the USER directive switches away from root. Pattern: `USER root` -> `RUN mkdir -p ${PROJECT_ROOT}/warehouse && chown -R <runtime-user>:root ${PROJECT_ROOT} && chmod 775 ${PROJECT_ROOT}` -> `USER <runtime-user>`. Otherwise any runtime path the LLD anchors on PATIENT360_PROJECT_ROOT that doesn't have its own bind mount becomes unwritable.

correction: Generated transform_patients.py defined `_bronze_path(env)` and `_silver_target_path(env)` as RELATIVE paths. Spark resolved them against spark-submit CWD (/opt/airflow), not against PATIENT360_PROJECT_ROOT. Reads 404'd while Bronze (post-pivot) wrote absolute paths under /opt/patient_360/warehouse/dev/bronze/. Same root cause hit the dq_rules_dir path which silver also passed as relative.
pattern: Every Silver/Gold layer module MUST emit ABSOLUTE Spark read/write paths anchored on `os.environ.get('PATIENT360_PROJECT_ROOT', '.')` (or PATIENT360_WAREHOUSE_ROOT once first-class). NEVER pass a relative path to spark.read.load / spark.write.save / spark.sql with a FROM clause — Airflow's spark-submit CWD is unpredictable (typically /opt/airflow). For DQ rules: prefer NOT passing dq_rules_dir at all; let se_runner._resolve_dq_rules_dir use the DQ_RULES_DIR env var (set by docker-compose to /opt/patient_360/dq_rules). If you must pass it, anchor on PATIENT360_PROJECT_ROOT. Enforces LLD v1.15 §9.1.

correction: Generated reconciliation.py kept the pre-pivot `uc_uri: str | None = None` parameter and called `build_spark(app_name=..., uc_uri=uc_uri)`. After the 2026-05-12 LLD §13 Decision 12 pivot removed UC from the runtime path, `build_spark()` lost the uc_uri kwarg. Reconciliation task failed with `TypeError: build_spark() got an unexpected keyword argument 'uc_uri'`.
pattern: When any architectural decision (LLD §13) revokes a runtime dependency, every generated file that referenced the removed dependency MUST be re-derived in the same chain. The create-/update-dag skills MUST include `src/<project>/bronze/reconciliation.py` (and any sibling reconciliation modules) in their AC deliverable lists alongside the DAG file itself, so route-out checks dispatch the file to update-ingestion (or own the module directly). NEVER let the reconciliation Python module fall through routing because the story's ACs only list the DAG file.

correction: Revoked 2026-05-22 direct-edit of scd2.py target_table kwarg + CREATE TABLE first-run branch per LLD v1.16 Decision 17; UC registration is now deploy-time only via make bootstrap-uc. STORY-03-001 AC8-AC10 implemented: removed target_table kwarg, removed runtime CREATE TABLE/CREATE SCHEMA from scd2.py + transform_patients.py, switched MERGE/SELECT to delta.`<path>` syntax, added lock-in unit test test_no_runtime_ddl_in_silver_sources.
pattern: Silver-layer helpers and transforms MUST NOT issue runtime catalog DDL (CREATE TABLE / CREATE SCHEMA / saveAsTable). Path-based Delta writes only; UC FQN visibility is established at deploy time via make bootstrap-uc per LLD v1.16 Decision 17. Every Silver source file in scope of Decision 17 must carry a lock-in pytest that greps for forbidden tokens.

correction: LLD v1.17 Decision 17 first selected a Spark-DDL bootstrap (one-shot UCSingleCatalog for CREATE TABLE only). Generated bootstrap_uc_tables.py fell over with java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'void org.apache.spark.internal.LogKey.$init$' the moment it called CREATE TABLE. Root cause: io.unitycatalog:unitycatalog-spark_2.13:0.3.0 (latest on Maven Central as of 2026-05-23) is compiled against Spark 3.5.x; the project runs PySpark 4.0.x. The LogKey trait was restructured between Spark 3.5 and Spark 4.0. UCSingleCatalog cannot be used with Spark 4.x AT ALL — not for DDL, not for writes, not for reads. This is the SAME binary-compat issue that motivated LLD §13 Decision 12 in 2026-05-12 (UCSingleCatalog out of the runtime write path). v1.17 underestimated that DDL-only operations hit the same wall.
pattern: NEVER select any Spark integration that requires io.unitycatalog:unitycatalog-spark when the project runs Spark 4.x. The artifact lineage (0.2.0, 0.2.1, 0.3.0) is Spark 3.5.x only; no Spark 4 build has been published as of 2026-05-23. For UC OSS table registration on a Spark 4.x stack, use the pure-Python REST API (POST /api/2.1/unity-catalog/{schemas,tables}) per LLD v1.18 Decision 17 Revised — zero Spark dependency. ALWAYS verify Maven Central artifact compatibility against the project's Spark major version BEFORE selecting a Spark-coupled bootstrap path in an LLD decision.

correction: During LLD v1.17 bring-up, two generator gaps surfaced before the architectural pivot to REST: (a) _spark_type helper in bootstrap_uc_tables.py only mapped bare type names (int, varchar, etc.) and failed loudly on parameterized SQL standard types from contracts/*.yml (VARCHAR(N), CHAR(N), DECIMAL(p,s)); (b) SparkSession builder set spark.sql.extensions=DeltaSparkSessionExtension but not spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog=DeltaCatalog, which Delta's CREATE TABLE planner requires. Both were direct-edited 2026-05-23 then made moot by the v1.18 REST pivot.
pattern: When generating a one-shot Spark application that touches Delta: ALWAYS set BOTH spark.sql.extensions=io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension AND spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog=org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog — Delta's CREATE/MERGE planner rejects sessions that have only the extension. When generating a contract-driven schema helper: ALWAYS pass through parameterized SQL standard types verbatim (VARCHAR(N), CHAR(N), DECIMAL(p,s), NUMERIC(p,s)) — these are Spark SQL native. The generator's type map should only need bare names; parameterized types should be passthrough.

correction: Default uc_bootstrap_uri 'http://unity-catalog:8080' (LLD v1.16/v1.17 §7.1) failed on host-side `make bootstrap-uc` with java.net.UnresolvedAddressException — the hostname only resolves inside the compose network. Updated to 'http://localhost:8080' in v1.18; STAGING/PROD configs keep the in-network hostname.
pattern: When generating defaults for any container-network service URL consumed by a host-side Make target: use the host-reachable form (localhost:<exposed-port>) for the DEV/host config, the in-network form (service-name:<container-port>) for STAGING/PROD or compose-internal callers. Document the choice in the LLD §7 config block. The exposed port comes from docker-compose ports: '<host>:<container>' mapping — generate from that, not from the EXPOSE / internal port.

correction: SCD2 silver transforms MUST dedupe source DataFrame to one row per natural key before invoking apply_scd2. Bronze accumulates one snapshot per ds partition; same natural key appears N times across N partition days. MERGE INTO fails with DELTA_MULTIPLE_SOURCE_ROW_MATCHING_TARGET_ROW_IN_MERGE on the 2nd run (the 1st run masks via cold-warehouse overwrite path). Confirmed 2026-05-23 by DAG run manual_ld_20260523T222531Z silver_dimensions.transform_patients_silver task.
pattern: row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY <natural_key> ORDER BY ds DESC) == 1 — apply in caller immediately before apply_scd2; fall back to _ingested_at if ds absent; raise ValueError if neither column exists. apply_scd2 stays caller-deduplicates per DMS §6 and LLD v1.18 §2.3.
